items.title: Live: US warships cross Strait of Hormuz amid crucial peace talks
items.description: Peace talks between the US and Iran are underway, after US Vice-President JD Vance touched down in Islamabad, Pakistan. Follow live.

items.title: Government launches multi-million-dollar fuel saving campaign
items.description: The federal government is launching a multi-million-dollar advertising campaign encouraging Australians to reduce car use as the global oil crisis persists.

items.title: In the Gulf, states are 'paying the price' for a war they didn't start
items.description: When the Iran war ends, Gulf nations will not only have to repair the economic and physical damage caused by Iran's retaliatory campaign, but will also have to learn to live with a regime that analysts say is "less predictable and more violent than it was two months ago".

items.title: 'They were already out of their seats': The moment Artemis II astronauts knew they were home safe
items.description: Nine days, one hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds, a journey deeper into space than ever before and a rapt Earth watching on. This is how four astronauts made history.

items.title: Artemis II was a product of politics. Then it sent us over the Moon
items.description: In both 1968 and 2026, a mission to the Moon offered a refreshing blast of positivity for a conflict-ridden world. So what's different now — and what do we really gain from this new moonshot, five decades after the first?

items.title: Kennedy breaks 10 seconds again to claim first national title in men's 100m
items.description: Lachlan Kennedy has stormed to victory in the men's 100m final at the Australian Athletics Championships in Sydney, equalling his personal best of 9.96 seconds.

items.title: How craft beer is changing China, one schooner at a time
items.description: On a midsummer night last year, I took a sip of lager at a craft beer pub in my hometown in China's south. But this was not just a beer. It was a cultural symbol that shows just how much China's Gen Z is changing.

items.title: A budget 'leak' so good, the journalist's editors didn't believe it
items.description: It was "the best Canberra scoop in years", but the journalist's own editors did not believe it, and almost buried the story.

items.title: Forget the manosphere: The nannasphere is an antidote to the horrors
items.description: Surely one of the best ways to counter the hate, grief and horrors of the world is to foster communities driven by decency, calm and care. Enter: the nannasphere.

items.title: Lying immobile after a remote chopper crash, Fred felt something biting his leg
items.description: In the aftermath of a 2019 helicopter crash in Kakadu National Park, Fred Hunter lay on the ground covered in blood and fuel, when he felt something biting his leg. On the 20th anniversary of CareFlight, Mr Hunter recounts his dramatic rescue by the service.

items.title: Hawks end Bulldogs unbeaten run in brilliant Gather Round performance
items.description: Hawthorn delivers a brilliant Gather Round performance to end the Bulldogs unbeaten run, after the Swans beat the Suns at Norwood Oval.

items.title: Four straight losses and 88 points in a fortnight sends Storm to rock bottom
items.description: The Warriors have ended their decade-long run of outs against Melbourne in style as the Storm officially hit rock bottom following a heavy loss.

items.title: 'We matter; we're important': Disabled artists centrestage in new show
items.description: Paper dolls, wrestlers and cloudscapes appear in an exhibition by a Western Sydney artist collective at Bathurst Regional Art Gallery.

items.title: Still trying to prove you're good at trivia? You're not fooling me
items.description: I applaud your courage for having a go at this quiz. That's about it, though.

items.title: 'I sound like a woman now': Why Katy Steele is reimagining her past
items.description: The Little Birdy frontwoman is getting in touch with her old self on her new album and tour.

items.title: Thai fishing port highlights 'big trouble' caused by Middle East war
items.description: Tens of thousands of small and commercial fishing vessels in Thailand are stranded on shore, no longer able to afford diesel, which has more than doubled in price since the Iran war began.

items.title: Hollingsworth 'moving on' from DQ then reinstatement as national champion
items.description: Claudia Hollingsworth insists she ran a fair race, and wants to move on from the drama surrounding the women's 1,500 metres final which saw her disqualified then reinstated, as Jess Hull crashed out.

items.title: Stolen car used by Sydney men in police chase linked to 'number of shootings'
items.description: The occupants of the allegedly stolen Audi threw fuel jerry cans and bleach containers from the car while trying to evade police, officers say.

items.title: 'Sounds good to me': How Trump was sold war in Iran
items.description: Extraordinary reporting reveals how Israel made the case for regime change in Iran — and how the fallout is driving a profound shift in American opinion, amid deep uncertainty about what the war has achieved.

items.title: War hero's looming prosecution divides opinion
items.description: Once celebrated as Australia's most decorated living war hero, the looming prosecution of Ben Roberts-Smith is shaping up to be the next trial of the century.

items.title: Teen shuns screens to turn love of chickens into growing egg business
items.description: While many teenagers spend their spare time online gaming or playing sport, 14-year-old Max Lye hangs out with a bunch of chooks and dreams of owning his own egg farm.

items.title: Maila may be just a tropical low by the time it reaches Australia
items.description: After causing damage to islands in the Pacific, Cyclone Maila is downgraded as it heads towards Australia.

items.title: Man dead as house destroyed in fire in Brisbane's south
items.description: Emergency services were called to a house fire on the corner of Foote and Annear streets in Acacia Ridge, where a man's body was found.

items.title: Milk prices may need to increase to cover soaring fuel and fertiliser costs
items.description: Dairy farmers across Australia are battling crippling fuel and fertiliser costs. The industry is now calling for a 30-cent-per-litre rise in milk prices on supermarket shelves.

items.title: Australians less likely to get bypass surgery now than 20 years ago
items.description: John Ross may be Australia's longest surviving double bypass patient. Here's how has the cardiac operation has evolved over the past 50 years.
